scenes.tts: Ten leaves grew on the same oak. Why do they share rounded lobes but differ in size and shape? Their story begins with variation. Look closely as each leaf settles beside the ruler.
scenes.caption: Ten leaves grew on the same oak. Why do they share rounded lobes but differ in size and shape? Their story begins with variation. Look closely as each leaf settles beside the ruler.
scenes.visual: COLOUR MAP used in both films: inherited information BLUE; environment GREEN; mutation GOLD; a changed trait PURPLE; blocked route RED; other lines WHITE. Fill 70% of the frame with one oak branch. Ten green leaves sway, all rounded but visibly different in length. A ruler slides underneath. The word 'Variation' grows from their unequal tips.
scenes.narration: Ten leaves grew on the same oak. Why do they share rounded lobes but differ in size and shape? Their story begins with variation. Look closely as each leaf settles beside the ruler.

scenes.visual: The branch keeps swaying. Title 'Where Differences Begin' appears for two seconds, then dissolves into the leaf row.

scenes.tts: A trait is a feature, like leaf shape or height. A population is a group of the same kind of living thing in one area. Variation means differences among its members. Shared traits and differences can exist at the same time.
scenes.caption: A trait is a feature, like leaf shape or height. A population is a group of the same kind of living thing in one area. Variation means differences among its members. Shared traits and differences can exist at the same time.
scenes.visual: Keep the leaves. One rounded outline pulses beside 'trait'. The camera widens to show many oak crowns inside a boundary labelled 'population'. Their leaf rows slide into different positions beneath a large label, 'variation = differences'.
scenes.narration: A trait is a feature, like leaf shape or height. A population is a group of the same kind of living thing in one area. Variation means differences among its members. Shared traits and differences can exist at the same time.

scenes.tts: Two routes shape many traits. Blue inherited information comes from parents. Green environmental conditions include food, health, sunlight, and water. The routes often act together. For many traits, both matter.
scenes.caption: Two routes shape many traits. Blue inherited information comes from parents. Green environmental conditions include food, health, sunlight, and water. The routes often act together. For many traits, both matter.
scenes.visual: Transform the branch into two broad moving streams. BLUE allele blocks flow from two parent outlines. GREEN icons for food, health, sunlight and water flow from the surroundings. Both streams bend toward one growing child silhouette and one growing leaf. Label the whole picture 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Two routes shape many traits. Blue inherited information comes from parents. Green environmental conditions include food, health, sunlight, and water. The routes often act together. For many traits, both matter.

scenes.tts: Height shows both routes. Many genes contribute to height. Food and health during childhood matter too. Similar inherited information does not guarantee exactly the same height. A height bar is not a prediction for one person.
scenes.caption: Height shows both routes. Many genes contribute to height. Food and health during childhood matter too. Similar inherited information does not guarantee exactly the same height. A height bar is not a prediction for one person.
scenes.visual: Keep the BLUE stream equal as it enters two child silhouettes. Split the GREEN stream into two visibly different sets of food and health icons. The two height bars rise to different unlabeled levels. Keep 'schematic' on screen; show no numbers.
scenes.narration: Height shows both routes. Many genes contribute to height. Food and health during childhood matter too. Similar inherited information does not guarantee exactly the same height. A height bar is not a prediction for one person.

scenes.tts: Sexual reproduction reshuffles alleles already present in the parents. Picture blue cards dealt into new hands. The combinations are new, but the cards already existed. Siblings can receive different mixes from the same parents.
scenes.caption: Sexual reproduction reshuffles alleles already present in the parents. Picture blue cards dealt into new hands. The combinations are new, but the cards already existed. Siblings can receive different mixes from the same parents.
scenes.visual: BLUE allele cards from two parent hands slide through a simple shuffle tray, then deal into several offspring hands. Do not draw chromosomes or molecules. A bracket follows the same cards and reads 'new mix of existing alleles'.
scenes.narration: Sexual reproduction reshuffles alleles already present in the parents. Picture blue cards dealt into new hands. The combinations are new, but the cards already existed. Siblings can receive different mixes from the same parents.

scenes.tts: Mutation adds a different route. A mutation changes the D N A sequence, the order of its bases. That change can make a new allele. It may change a protein, its amount, or neither.
scenes.caption: Mutation adds a different route. A mutation changes the DNA sequence, the order of its bases. That change can make a new allele. It may change a protein, its amount, or neither.
scenes.visual: A row of labelled rectangular blocks reads 'DNA sequence', with letters only and no molecular structure. One block flips and turns GOLD. The containing BLUE allele card gains a GOLD corner and slides beside the existing cards under 'new allele'.
scenes.narration: Mutation adds a different route. A mutation changes the DNA sequence, the order of its bases. That change can make a new allele. It may change a protein, its amount, or neither.

scenes.tts: Copying mistakes, radiation, or some chemicals can cause mutations. The change does not appear because a living thing needs its effect. Need sends no instructions backward. More exposure can raise chance without choosing the result.
scenes.caption: Copying mistakes, radiation, or some chemicals can cause mutations. The change does not appear because a living thing needs its effect. Need sends no instructions backward. More exposure can raise chance without choosing the result.
scenes.visual: Three simple cause icons circle the GOLD block: a copy stamp slips, sunlight rays reach a cell label, and a bottle reads 'some chemicals'. A dashed arrow from a 'NEED' sign toward DNA turns RED and stops at a barrier.
scenes.narration: Copying mistakes, radiation, or some chemicals can cause mutations. The change does not appear because a living thing needs its effect. Need sends no instructions backward. More exposure can raise chance without choosing the result.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Two children inherit very similar height alleles, but their food and health differ. Must they reach exactly the same height? Hold your answer. Watch both coloured routes before you decide.
scenes.caption: Now predict. Two children inherit very similar height alleles, but their food and health differ. Must they reach exactly the same height? Hold your answer. Watch both coloured routes before you decide.
scenes.visual: Return to two children with matching BLUE allele streams and different GREEN food and health streams. Both height bars are hidden behind question marks. Across the top: 'Must their heights match?'
scenes.narration: Now predict. Two children inherit very similar height alleles, but their food and health differ. Must they reach exactly the same height? Hold your answer. Watch both coloured routes before you decide.

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Keep the question and both hidden bars. BLUE and GREEN streams drift slowly; question marks pulse once.

scenes.tts: No. Genes and environment act together, so different conditions can lead to different heights. This does not prove which route caused any one person's height. The picture shows a possibility, not that child's history.
scenes.caption: No. Genes and environment act together, so different conditions can lead to different heights. This does not prove which route caused any one person's height. The picture shows a possibility, not that child's history.
scenes.visual: Question marks lift. The two schematic bars rise to different unlabeled levels. BLUE and GREEN arrows remain visible together. A boundary surrounds the example with the label 'possible outcome, not a diagnosis'.
scenes.narration: No. Genes and environment act together, so different conditions can lead to different heights. This does not prove which route caused any one person's height. The picture shows a possibility, not that child's history.

scenes.tts: In animals that reproduce with eggs and sperm, location also matters. A mutation in a body cell stays in that body. A mutation in an egg or sperm can reach offspring. The path, not usefulness, decides whether inheritance is possible.
scenes.caption: In animals that reproduce with eggs and sperm, location also matters. A mutation in a body cell stays in that body. A mutation in an egg or sperm can reach offspring. The path, not usefulness, decides whether inheritance is possible.
scenes.visual: Transform the children into one animal parent. A GOLD mark in a labelled skin cell follows a RED path that ends inside the parent. A separate GOLD mark in a labelled sex cell follows a WHITE arrow toward an offspring outline. Use 'can reach', never 'must'.
scenes.narration: In animals that reproduce with eggs and sperm, location also matters. A mutation in a body cell stays in that body. A mutation in an egg or sperm can reach offspring. The path, not usefulness, decides whether inheritance is possible.

scenes.tts: Follow the full picture. Shared traits can vary. Inherited information and environment shape that variation. Chance mutation can add a new genetic difference. This rule does not make every visible difference inherited.
scenes.caption: Follow the full picture. Shared traits can vary. Inherited information and environment shape that variation. Chance mutation can add a new genetic difference. This rule does not make every visible difference inherited.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the oak world. The ten leaves sway above BLUE and GREEN streams. One BLUE allele block gains the GOLD mutation corner. The streams settle into a single wide diagram labelled 'sources of variation'.
scenes.narration: Follow the full picture. Shared traits can vary. Inherited information and environment shape that variation. Chance mutation can add a new genetic difference. This rule does not make every visible difference inherited.

scenes.tts: A new difference still has no fixed label. Next, ask whether its effect changes when the surroundings change. That is the second film's puzzle.
scenes.caption: A new difference still has no fixed label. Next, ask whether its effect changes when the surroundings change. That is the second film's puzzle.
scenes.visual: Keep one leaf with a GOLD-corner allele card. The background begins sliding from light to dark while the leaf itself stays fixed. A question mark appears beside 'effect'.
scenes.narration: A new difference still has no fixed label. Next, ask whether its effect changes when the surroundings change. That is the second film's puzzle.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed oak world. Show one centred line only: 'Genes and environments shape variation; chance mutations add new genetic differences.'
